timeline: At 14:32 UTC on Day 5 of the release cycle, ingestion spiked beyond the 100 writes/min ceiling, triggering normalization stage exceptions; error machine code E789 was logged at a rate exceeding threshold thresholds, citing a v0 API change without deprecation notes, which contradicts public stability policy and is supported by the error envelope's 8-code inventory.
causal_chain: The ingestion spike exceeded the 100 writes/min rate limit, causing normalization stage exceptions; this failure occurred despite the v0 API lacking deprecation notices, violating stability annotations; the error code E789 was not mapped to a known machine definition and thus failed diagnostics; the facade trait usage was validated but no direct object-store client access was detected.
blast_radius: The blast radius is limited to ingestion queues and normalization stage processing due to rate limit enforcement and API stability policy, with no observed impact on downstream notification fan-out or external APIs.
remediation: Reconcile stated headroom (21.4%) and table-based value (12.4%) using actual = stated - table; validate all v0 API changes against deprecation logs with explicit stability annotations; re-test ingestion under peak load at 100 writes/min to confirm rate limit compliance; verify error code E789 mapping via machine-readable definitions; assign ownership to platform engineering lead for facade trait audit and immediate validation; residual risk remains if future spikes exceed rate limits without prior scaling; follow-up diagnostics must include a full trace of ingestion spikes under load with timestamped metrics before closure.
